- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for potential rebound.  
- Model consistently underestimates prices after recent spikes (e.g., >70) — add 3–5% buffer to forecast for 3–5 days post-spike.  
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing mean reversion — if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should be slightly above recent low to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum — if sentiment is trending upward, forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% per day for first 3–5 days.  
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts when sentiment is mixed (±0.33) — use conservative midpoint between recent high and low.
